title: Warm Handoff & Embedded CS Plan — First 3 Months (Sprint Template)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, action-oriented template for the customer success (CS) warm-handoff and embedded onboarding sprint covering the customer’s first 3 months post-contract. Intended for CSMs + Solutions Engineers to coordinate execution, track adoption signals, and flag renewal triggers early.

Status: DRAFT — iterative. Use for high-touch customers or any pilot where embedding engineers/CS into the account for 30–90 days is required.

Top-level goals (aligned to renewal outcomes):
1) Realize 1–2 measurable product-led value moments in first 30 days (e.g., production inference flow running, embedding pipeline smoke test, dashboarding baseline).
2) Achieve predictable monthly usage baseline and adoption funnel (calls/day or tokens/month depending on product).
3) Remove key technical blockers so the customer can self-serve critical flows by month 3.
4) Identify renewal health signals and surface expansion opportunities by day 60.

Ownership & Roles (example):
- CSM (primary): owns adoption plan, executive check-ins, renewal prep.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): technical onboarding, runbooks, integration checkpoints.
- Customer Engineering (customer contact): implements SDKs, infra work, SSO.
- Product Ops: monitors analytics and surfaces regressions.
- Account Exec (AM): commercial touchpoint on business outcomes.

Warm-handoff checklist (immediately upon deal close):
- [ ] Account summary doc from AE (contract scope, SKUs, seats, timelines).
- [ ] Technical intake form completed (deployment mode: hosted/dedicated/private; region; data residency; SSO/KMS).
- [ ] Access granted: API keys, Console invites, Slack channel created.
- [ ] Kickoff meeting scheduled (within 3 business days).
- [ ] Initial success metrics defined (baseline + target).

Sprint structure overview (weekly cadence):
- Week 0: Kickoff + environment access (goal: first successful API call or integration smoke test).
- Weeks 1–4 (Embed sprint 1): Get 1st production path working, surface blockers, quick wins.
- Weeks 5–8 (Scale sprint 2): Harden reliability, enable telemetry, optimize cost controls.
- Weeks 9–12 (Handover sprint 3): Transition playbooks, train internal ops, finalize renewal/expansion plan.

30-day checklist (priority: unblock production):
- Technical:
  - [ ] API integration complete (test -> staging).
  - [ ] Authentication & permissions validated (SSO, API keys).
  - [ ] Sample prompts and eval prompt set uploaded to console for quality monitoring.
  - [ ] Cost guardrails configured (quotas, soft alerts).
- Adoption:
  - [ ] 2 product champions identified and added to weekly sync.
  - [ ] Internal team training session (recording + slides).
- Business:
  - [ ] First value metric measured and accepted by customer (e.g., query latency < 500ms, throughput N req/min).

60-day checklist (priority: scale predictably):
- Technical:
  - [ ] Autoscaling policy validated with load test (SE-run).
  - [ ] Caching/prefix strategies evaluated.
  - [ ] Observability: token-level cost breakdown enabled, key traces connected.
- Adoption:
  - [ ] 3+ internal users actively using product week-over-week.
  - [ ] 1 internal integration (e.g., CRM, search) returns live data with embeddings.
- Business:
  - [ ] Usage baseline defined (tokens/month, calls/day) and agreed for renewal health.

90-day checklist (priority: self-serve + renewal prep):
- Technical:
  - [ ] Handoff runbook and escalation matrix published in customer Confluence.
  - [ ] Backup model variant(s) and fallback routes configured.
  - [ ] Cost/perf optimization suggestions implemented (quantization/batching where applicable).
- Adoption:
  - [ ] Internal ops trained and confident to run incident playbook.
  - [ ] Regular usage report automated to exec stakeholders.
- Renewal prep:
  - [ ] Health scorecard (traffic, latency, cost, quality) ready for QBR.
  - [ ] Renewal risks flagged and mitigation plan drafted.

Renewal signals & early warning triggers (watch for these):
- Negative signals:
  - Sudden drop in daily requests >25% without seasonality.
  - Persistent quality regressions tracked by eval set.
  - Unresolved billing/quotas disputes.
- Positive signals:
  - Sustained 20%+ weekly growth in core metric for 4+ weeks.
  - Internal RJ (reference job) created and shared by customer.

Quick templates (copy-paste examples):
- 3-day kickoff agenda:
  1) Intros + success definitions (10m)
  2) Contract & scope review (5m)
  3) Architecture and access checklist (20m)
  4) First-steps runbook + immediate owners (15m)
  5) Next steps + action items (10m)

- Post-kickoff email snippet:
  Subject: Next steps from kickoff — [Account] / Redwood
  Hi [Name],
  Thanks for today — attaching the action tracker and access steps. Owner for each action inlined. Target for first smoke test: [date].
  Action tracker: [link]

Risks & mitigation (notes to self):
- If SE bandwidth limited, prioritize a 2-hour remote pairing session to unblock integration rather than multiple async tickets.
- If customer requires private deployment, confirm timeline for infra & security sign-off early (this kills velocity if delayed).
- TODO: finalize a short-run SLO checklist for Dedicated customers (low-effort doc).

Renewal tracker (simple table — fill during sprints):
| Metric | Baseline | Target by 90d | Current | Risk | Owner |
| Tokens/mo | 0 | 150k | 18k | Medium | CSM |
| Core calls/day | 0 | 500 | 42 | High (infra) | SE |
| Exec sponsor active | No | Yes | No | High | AM |

Signals mapping (how we score health):
- Green: Usage >70% of target AND no open P1s for 14d.
- Yellow: Usage 40–70% OR 1 unresolved P1 in last 14d.
- Red: Usage <40% OR >1 P1 OR exec sponsor disengaged.

Notes for QBR prep (end of month 3):
- Bring a 1-pager with: usage trend, cost vs expectations, top 3 wins, open risks, and next steps.
- Include engineering ask backlog and estimated lift for expansion items.

Playbook snippets (short):
- If model quality drops after a deploy: revert to previous model variant (documented in rollout), open regression ticket, run eval set to quantify impact, notify CSM+SE.
- If cost suddenly spikes: pause heavy batch jobs, enable stricter quotas, and schedule emergency cost review with customer.

Metrics & instrumentation (minimum telemetry to enable):
- Daily tokens and calls per route.
- 95th/99th latency per route.
- Error rates and P1/P2 incidents.
- Eval-set quality score over time.
- Token-level cost and per-route spend (for cost attribution).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we include a lightweight SOC2 checklist for private deployments in this template? (depends how often customers ask).
- Add a one-pager for partner-delivered onboarding (if SE time not available).
- Convert renewal tracker to sheet with conditional formatting (owner: Data Ops).

References & links:
- CS onboarding playbook (internal): https://redwood.atl/confluence/display/CS/Onboarding+Playbook
- SE runbooks repo: github.com/redwood/se-onboarding
- Related Jira tickets: JIRA-CS-4321 (warm handoff improvements), JIRA-CS-4412 (renewal scoring update)

End of doc — use this as a living template. Copy per account and replace placeholders.
